body:
`actions/setup-python` accepts `python-version: "3.x"` to mean "latest stable Python 3.y at run time". `uv` has no equivalent — `uv python install "3.x"` is rejected outright ("not a valid Python download request"), and a bare major version like `uv python install 3` / `uv sync --python 3` prefers reusing whatever already satisfies the request over fetching the newest, so it doesn't reliably track "latest" either.

This came up setting up a CI job whose only job is a platform smoke test (Windows-only stdio bug check) — the exact Python version genuinely doesn't matter, we just want "whatever is current" without bumping a pin every time a new minor ships. Ended up working around it by running `actions/setup-python` with `"3.x"` first just to resolve a concrete version, then handing that to `uv sync --python <resolved>` — works, but it's an odd thing to need a second tool for.

Would `uv python install`/`uv sync --python` (and `.python-version`) accepting something like `3.x`, or a `latest` keyword, be in scope? Happy to be pointed at prior discussion if this has already been considered and rejected.
title: Support a "latest Python 3.x" version request (like setup-python's "3.x")
